newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed manufacturing index up to 125.3 in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed manufacturing index up to 125.3 in Feb.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago said its Chicago Fed Midwest Manufacturing Index (CFMMI) rose 1.1 percent to a record 125.3 in February from a revised 124.0 in January.

For the first time since July 1996, all sectors of the CFMMI posted positive monthly growth, the report said. In addition, all sectors except machinery outperformed the Federal Reserve's national industrial production index for manufacturing.
The steel sector index rose most strongly, climbing 2.1 percent in February to 132.4 from 129.6.

"While this was the steel sector's largest increase since September 1995, it comes on the heals of a 0.8 percent decline in January, a weakness attributable to outages that occurred at several of the region's steel mills," the report said.
Turning to other components, the auto index rose to 135.7 from 133.7, the machinery index climbed to 140.7 from 139.5 and the resource index grew to 112.0 from 111.4.
The Federal Reserve's industrial production index for manufacturing rose to 119.8 in February from 118.9 the month before.
